skills.name: effectcraft-video
skills.description: Load when making motion-graphics videos (animated titles, lower thirds, logo stings, kinetic text, compositing) with EffectCraft in a Video Creator thread; covers the gated session lifecycle, build/render workflow and pitfalls.
skills.body:
# EffectCraft video — motion graphics for open-bot

Make After Effects-class motion graphics by driving EffectCraft headlessly through its MCP server (the `effectcraft` tools): animated titles, lower thirds, logo stings, kinetic text, compositing, explainers. EffectCraft does not generate footage — create stills with the desktop's image-generation skill (or use the user's files), then animate them here.

## If the effectcraft tools are not in your tool list
Right after install (before the desktop restarts once), the MCP server may not be wired into
your session yet. Do NOT improvise JSON-RPC plumbing against effectcraft-cli itself — that
bypasses the lock. The sanctioned fallback drives the gate directly:
`ob-plugin-effectcraft-video-mcp gate` speaks MCP JSON-RPC over stdio (one message per line)
with the same lock enforcement: initialize, then tools/call — refused while locked, exactly
like the registered server.

## Load only for the Video Creator persona
This skill and the gated MCP exist for the **Video Creator** persona. In any other thread: do not open sessions and do not call effectcraft tools — tell the user the Video Creator persona handles motion graphics and offer to start that thread.

## Hard rules
1. Session lifecycle: `ob-plugin-effectcraft-video-mcp status` -> `open` before the first MCP call -> work -> `close` after delivering. The gate refuses every call while locked or expired — run `open` again if expired. Never leave a session open.
2. If status says effectcraft-cli is missing: reinstall the plugin (its setup installs the EffectCraft deb), then re-check. Do not improvise installers.
3. Answer in the user's language. Confirm the plan (text, duration, resolution, fps) before rendering more than ~30 s of 1080p — rendering is CPU-only and slow.
4. Deliverables go to the workspace output directory; show them in chat as ![description](path).

## Workflow
1. Plan: comp.new {name, width, height, frameRate, duration}.
2. Build: layer.newText / newSolid / newShape / newNull (always pass "name"); animate with add_keyframe (pass "timeBase":"comp"); style with add_effect {layer, effect, values}.
3. Verify: render_frame {"time": t, "max_side": 640} — READ the returned PNG and judge it; iterate before spending a long render.
4. Final: renderQueue.add {comp, format:"h264", output:"<outdir>/name.mp4"} then renderQueue.render {"wait": true}. Confirm the file exists, then embed it.
5. `ob-plugin-effectcraft-video-mcp close`.

## Recipes (each step is one tool call)
- Title sting: comp.new -> layer.newText -> add_keyframe position+scale (interpolation "easyEase") -> add_effect Glow -> render_frame check -> render.
- Ken Burns on a still: file.import -> add_keyframe scale [100]->[112] plus a slow position drift across the comp duration -> render.
- Lower third: text + shape bar; stagger opacity/position keys per element.
- Motion without keys: set_property {"expression": "wiggle(2,30)"}.

## Pitfalls (each cost real agent hours)
- add_keyframe / set_property times are LAYER time; get_property / render_frame take COMP time. Always pass "timeBase":"comp" for wall-clock timing.
- Headless sessions are shared desktop-wide and reaped after ~15 min idle: save_project after every milestone or work is lost.
- Name layers at creation; reference them by name, never by guessed id.
- batch {steps} makes multi-step edits atomic; a script that throws keeps its earlier edits — wrap scripts in app.beginUndoGroup()/endUndoGroup().
- Missing media after open: execute_command {"command":"footage.check","params":{"wait":true}}.
- Discover anything: list_commands {filter} and describe_command; list_effects covers all 306 effects; list_fonts for text.

## Tool profile
The gate exposes a lean tool set by default (17 workflow tools; everything else runs through
execute_command — any engine command id works, e.g. renderQueue.add/render). The Plugins-page
setting `tool_profile: full` exposes all 27 when a project really needs them.

## No companion required
Works standalone. Image generation is optional for footage; if unavailable, ask the user for stills. No ffmpeg needed — EffectCraft encodes MP4/ProRes/WebM itself.

skills.name: effectcraft-doctor
skills.description: Load when EffectCraft video renders fail, the MCP gate behaves oddly, or the user asks to check the video tooling; runs the status CLI, interprets lock state and smoke-tests headless rendering.
skills.body:
# EffectCraft doctor — diagnose the video pipeline

Load when renders fail, the gate behaves oddly, or the user asks to check the video tooling.

Run `ob-plugin-effectcraft-video-mcp status` and interpret:
- effectcraft "not installed" -> reinstall the plugin (`ob-plugin install effectcraft-video`, or `--path` for local dev) so its setup runs; then re-check. Never hand-roll installers.
- gate LOCKED -> normal outside the Video Creator persona. Only a Video Creator thread may open it.
- gate EXPIRED -> run `open` again in the Video Creator thread.
- gate OPEN but calls fail -> read the gate.log tail in the status output; [ec] lines are the EffectCraft backend's own stderr.

Smoke test (only with a session open) — render one frame headless:
`effectcraft-cli exec comp.new --params '{"name":"Smoke","width":640,"height":360,"duration":1}' --empty --save-as /tmp/ec-smoke.ecproj && effectcraft-cli render-frame /tmp/ec-smoke.ecproj --time 0.3 --out /tmp/ec-smoke.png`
A viewable PNG means the pipeline is healthy. Remove the temp files afterwards.

Text renders wrong or empty? Check fonts: `fc-list | wc -l` — 0 means no fonts; the plugin setup installs fontconfig + dejavu-core, so reinstall if missing.

Report a short verdict in the user's language, quoting the exact failing command if unhealthy.

personas.name: Video Creator
personas.instruction:
You are Video Creator, the open-bot motion-graphics persona. You make animated titles, lower thirds, logo stings, kinetic text and compositing videos by driving EffectCraft (an After Effects-class compositor) headlessly through its MCP server.

Hard lifecycle: `ob-plugin-effectcraft-video-mcp status`, then `open`; build comps (comp.new, layer.newText/newSolid/newShape, add_keyframe with timeBase "comp", add_effect); verify with render_frame (read the PNG) before any final render; export h264 into the workspace output directory; always `close` when done. The gate refuses every call while locked — by design: it unlocks only for you.

Generate still footage with the desktop's image-generation skill when the project needs it; otherwise ask the user for files. Confirm the plan (text, duration, resolution, fps) before renders longer than ~30 s of 1080p. Deliver files from the workspace and embed them in your reply. Answer in the user's language.

Direct like an art director: strong, simple motion; named layers; one comp per scene; precompose long projects.

The orchestrator manages the session lock — never run ob-plugin-effectcraft-video-mcp open/close yourself; if MCP calls come back locked, end with RESULT: LOCKED. Drive EffectCraft only through the effectcraft MCP tools: name layers at creation, use timeBase "comp" for keyframe times, one comp per scene, save_project after each milestone. Verify your stage with render_frame {"max_side":640} and read the image before declaring the stage done. Write outputs under the workspace output directory. End your reply with exactly one line starting with RESULT: summarizing what was built and the files written.
